title: Docs: re-anchor the file:line citations in docs/guide.md and docs/design.md
lead: Fix the `file:line` citations in `docs/guide.md` and `docs/design.md` that no longer point at the text they describe, and add a small stdlib test that every such citation still names a file and a line range that exist. Docs and one test file only; no behavior change.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Three later-notes rows report the same drift (owner, 2026-10-31: later-notes rows are folded into sweep slices; the folded sub-items are listed here so nothing is lost):
- S190 item 6: "guide.md sections 13/14 anchors drifted" (from the S168 review).
- S192 item 5: "docs/guide.md anchors to design.md drifted" (from the S174 review). S192 itself moved to v1.2 (owner, 2026-10-31); only this item is carried here.
- S193 item 1: "re-anchor the docs/guide.md citations into docs/design.md (lines 57, 64, 70, 77, 92, 95, 118) after S184 and S174".

A scan on 2026-10-31 (HEAD `2b6a27a`) found 72 `path:N[-M]` citations in `docs/guide.md` and 3 sibling-repo citations in `docs/design.md` (`agents/setup/lib/workflow-vendor.sh:22-41`, `slicer/docs/agents.md:712`, `slicer/docs/tui.md:183-270`; all three resolved by hand). None is out of range, but many point at other text. Examples confirmed by reading the cited line and `rg` for the right one:
- `docs/guide.md:331` cites `internal/tui/keys.go:80` for the `o` key; that line is `New`. `Owner` is at `internal/tui/keys.go:87`.
- `docs/guide.md:333` cites `internal/cli/cli.go:52` for `ork file RUN N`; it is at `:66`.
- `docs/guide.md:356` cites `internal/cli/cli.go:47-50` for `ork approve RUN`; it is at `:55-56`.
- `docs/guide.md:392` cites `internal/tui/keys.go:71` for the `c` cleanup key; `Cleanup` is at `:75`.
- `docs/guide.md:353` cites `docs/design.md:351-397` for landing; the `land` step starts at `docs/design.md:392` and runs to about `:432`.
- `docs/guide.md:361` cites `docs/design.md:390-397` for the landing conflict rule; that paragraph is at `docs/design.md:425-432`.
These are evidence, not the list: the implementer checks all of them again, because other v1.1 slices move lines in `docs/design.md`, `docs/dashboard.md`, `internal/cli/cli.go` and `internal/tui/keys.go`.

Line anchors drift every time a doc or a file above them grows. Whether to keep line anchors in guide.md at all, or to cite a section name for doc-to-doc references, is the owner's call (MANIFEST-E.md, DR-Q1). This outline keeps line anchors, as the guide does today, and adds a test that catches only gross drift (a file or line that no longer exists). The test cannot tell that a line moved to other text; the rg checks below are what does.

Nothing in slicer covers this: `slicer find re-anchor` and `slicer find anchors` list only done ork items (S87, S114, S115, S126, S127, S70, S112, S07, S27).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
N-class: no internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd path. It is docs and one test, so it can pair with any E-class slice.

- `docs/guide.md` (each wrong citation).
- `docs/design.md` (any in-repo citation that the scan finds wrong; the three sibling-repo citations at :793, :1440 and :1711 are checked and fixed only if wrong).
- `internal/docscheck/cite_test.go` (new; a test-only package, stdlib only).
- `CHANGELOG.md` (an entry under ## Unreleased).

Run this slice after the other v1.1 slices that edit `docs/design.md`, `docs/dashboard.md`, `docs/state.md`, `internal/cli/cli.go` or `internal/tui/keys.go`, and before the release-prep slice. If it runs earlier, the citations drift again. Do not pair it with a slice that edits `docs/guide.md` or `docs/design.md` heavily (the named wave, the engine rule and the landing check all do): two edits to the same lines conflict.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
The citation test passes before and after the fix, because every cited range exists today; it is a guard, not the failing test. What fails first is each wrong citation, shown by a check command whose output names a line that differs from the cited one. Before the fix, the cited line is wrong; after it, the command prints the cited line.

Checks to run now and again after the edit (the line numbers are those of HEAD `2b6a27a`; the implementer regenerates them):
- `rg -n '^\s+Owner:' internal/tui/keys.go` prints `87`; `docs/guide.md` must cite `internal/tui/keys.go:87` (not `:80`).
- `rg -n 'ork file RUN N' internal/cli/cli.go` prints `66`; the guide must cite `internal/cli/cli.go:66`.
- `rg -n 'ork approve RUN' internal/cli/cli.go` prints `55`; the guide must cite a range that includes `:55`.
- `rg -n '^\s+Cleanup:' internal/tui/keys.go` prints `75`; the guide must cite `:75`.
- `rg -n '^- \*\*land\*\*' docs/design.md` prints `392`; the landing citations (`docs/guide.md:19` and `:353`) must start there.
- `rg -n 'A merge conflict, or a red re-check' docs/design.md` prints `425`; the guide's conflict citation (`:361`) must start there.
- One such command for every other citation the implementer finds wrong, written into the commit message and the CHANGELOG entry as `citation: old -> new`.

`internal/docscheck/cite_test.go` (new):
- `TestGuideAndDesignCitationsResolve`: for each `path:N` or `path:N-M` in a backtick span in `docs/guide.md` and `docs/design.md`, the file exists under the repo root and `1 <= N <= M <= line count`. A path that starts with `slicer/`, `adjudicate/` or `agents/` is read from the sibling directory next to the repo (`../slicer/...`); the test skips such a citation with `t.Skip`-style logging when that directory is absent (CI has only this repo).
- `TestCitationParserHandlesRangesAndSuffixes`: `a.go:5`, `a.go:5-9`, `a.go:5-9,12` (the guide uses `pane.go:284-297,498`), and a citation inside prose with a trailing comma or parenthesis.
- `TestCitationTestFailsOnAMissingFile` and `...OnAnOutOfRangeLine`: the parser's checker, driven with temporary files.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Tests first for the parser; the doc edits follow the checks above.

1. List every citation: `rg -n -o '[A-Za-z0-9_./-]+\.(go|md|json|sh|yml|txt):[0-9]+(-[0-9]+)?' docs/guide.md docs/design.md`. For each, read the cited lines and decide whether they still hold the text the sentence describes (use `rg -n` for the symbol or phrase to find where it is now). Fix only the wrong ones. Do not rewrite surrounding text, and do not re-flow lines (keep lines at or under 80 columns where they are today).
2. Prefer the narrowest honest range: the line of the symbol, or the start and end of the section.
3. Add the test package. The parser should accept a range list such as `284-297,498` and check each part. No dependency beyond the standard library.
4. After the edit, re-run every check command in Failing tests and the full citation listing; write the fixed ones into the CHANGELOG entry. List any citation you could not decide in the commit message instead of guessing.
5. Do not touch code, other docs, or `docs/orchestrator-parity.md` and `docs/dashboard.md` citations (out of scope for the three folded notes).
6. CHANGELOG entry last, under `## Unreleased`: `Docs: ...` naming the files; add it as the final edit so a parallel slice's entry does not conflict.

Not a UI slice: no `internal/tui`, no golden view, no `ui.*` key, no CLI output.

Owner decisions (2026-11-11): How should the last Check line (the `git diff -U0 ... | rg ...` spot check) be run and judged? -> runnable form: the implementer runs the diff and reads every changed line by eye, with no pipe. The `rg` and pipeline form is outside the implementer's resolved allowlist, and the project `.claude/settings.json` has no `rg`, `git diff` or `go test` entry..

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `go test -race -count=1 ./...` (the new test included); `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`.
- Every command under Failing tests prints the line the doc now cites.
- `git diff --stat` lists only `docs/guide.md`, `docs/design.md`, `internal/docscheck/cite_test.go` and `CHANGELOG.md`.
- `git diff -U0 docs/guide.md docs/design.md | rg '^[-+]' | rg -v '`'` prints nothing that is not a changed citation line (spot check that no prose changed).

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch: "Docs: re-anchor file:line citations in the guide and design".
